correctness.rationale: For each edge, the orthogonal-projection condition is exactly the stated strip inequality. Strict satisfaction makes every edge foot an interior distance minimum and every vertex a distance maximum, so all \(2n\) faces give distinct normal bases. Conversely, \(2n\) distinct face-based normals require all edge strips. For odd \(n\), the strip directions give a regular \(2n\)-gon; for even \(n\), opposite edge tangents duplicate strips and give a regular \(n\)-gon. The radius comparisons place the chamber inside \(P_n\) for all admissible \(n\). The perimeter-times-inradius formulas yield the exact ratios; Taylor expansion yields the parity-dependent asymptotics. Finite numerical evaluations are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The maximal-normal locus area is a natural statistic complementary to average normal count: it answers how much of a regular polygon realizes the largest possible face-count bound. The exact parity split in the chamber shape and the fourth-order area coefficient is not recoverable from the maximum count alone, and provides a compact asymptotic comparison between even and odd regular polygons.
